Wiring & Assembly Guide

SkillGame · Wiring Diagram

How the machine connects: the mini-PC drives four FT232H USB boards; each reads the playfield switches or drives the score lamps / solenoids / NeoPixel strip. Signal flow, the four driver circuits, external power, the board with labels, and the full KiCad schematic.

System overview

One USB hub off the mini-PC feeds all four FT232H boards (told apart by their FTDI serial, GPIO1–GPIO4). Switches run on a 3.3 V supply; the NeoPixel strip on a 5 V supply; lamps and solenoids on their own supplies. Every ground is tied together.

The four driver circuits

Every connection is one of these four. (Simplified from your KiCad schematic — the full schematic is at the bottom.)

① Switch input — active-High

3.3 V→ hole switch→ FT232H pinDx / Cx→ 10 kΩ→ GND

Closing the hole switch pulls the pin to 3.3 V; the 10 kΩ holds it Low otherwise. Software reads "High" = pressed. The 7 gobble holes all wire to one pin (S23).

② Lamp driver — PN2222A (×16)

FT232H pinCx / Dx→ 1 kΩ→ PN2222Abase→ lamp→ lamp V+via J2

Pin High → transistor conducts → lamp lights. Emitter to GND. All score / indicator lamps use this, out through harness connector J2.

③ Solenoid driver — TIP120 + flyback (×2)

GPIO3 C0/C1→ 1 kΩ→ TIP120base→ solenoid coil→ solenoid V+fused

Higher-current TIP120 for the coils, with a 1N4004 across each coil to catch the flyback spike on release (fused via F1/F2). Coin-lock (C0) and win-lock (C1) only. Emitter to GND.

④ NeoPixel strip — WS2812b

GPIO4 D1SPI MOSI→ strip DIN
5 V→strip +5V GND→strip GND

Data only from GPIO4 D1 (MOSI), via the SPI1 / “5VDC” connector. Power the 150-pixel strip from the 5 V supply — never from USB.

External power & how it connects to the board

Five power domains. Everything shares one common ground — tie the USB/logic ground and every supply's ground together, or nothing will read/switch correctly.

SupplyVoltageBoard connectorPowers
Mini-PCUSB 5 VU1–U4 (USB)FT232H board logic (via the USB hub)
Wall PSU3.3 VJ1 “3VDC”the common side of every playfield switch
Wall PSU5 VSPI1 “5VDC”WS2812b strip (+5V); data comes from GPIO4 D1
Lamp PSUV+ (lamp)J2 harnessall score / indicator lamps (through PN2222A)
Solenoid PSUV+ (coil)solenoid conncoin-lock & win-lock coils (through TIP120, fused F1/F2)

The board, labeled

Top copper. Each FT232H socket (U1–U4) is silk-labeled with the serial that must go in it. Full pin-by-pin: SkillGame_GPIO_Map.html.

FT232H board pinout

Each of the four modules is this Adafruit FT232H breakout. D4–D7 / C0–C7 are the GPIO used here; D0–D3 are the SPI/MPSSE pins (only D1/MOSI is used, on GPIO4).

Wiring checklist

  • Serials first. Program each FT232H's serial to GPIO1…GPIO4 and seat it in the matching silk-labeled socket (U1–U4).
  • Common ground. Tie the USB logic ground and the 3.3 V, 5 V, lamp, and solenoid grounds together.
  • Switches to the input pins (each with its 10 kΩ pull-down); all 7 gobble holes parallel to one input (S23).
  • Lamps to J2; solenoids to the TIP120 outputs — confirm the 1N4004 flyback and fuses are fitted before powering the coils.
  • NeoPixel data to GPIO4 D1; power from the 5 V supply.
